$comment: Narrow permission allowlist so deploys run unattended. The rules and the
reason for every deny are documented in CLAUDE.md under 'What runs without
asking' -- this file is the enforcement and that section is the argument.
DENY TAKES PRECEDENCE OVER ALLOW. That is Claude Code's own rule, not
something this file arranges, and it is why the deny list can be written
broadly without having to reason about overlaps: 'make deploy*' is allowed
and 'anything containing systemctl --user restart' is denied, so a deploy
that grew a restart would be refused rather than inherited.
The allow list is a list of SHAPES, not of intentions. Each entry is
something whose worst case is known: a gate that reads, a git operation on a
repo whose history is recoverable, a deploy target whose whole body is fixed
and audited by tools/validate_deploy.py. Anything whose worst case depends on
its arguments stays behind a prompt.
EVERY make ENTRY IS MIRRORED BY THE FORM THAT RUNS WITHOUT make. `make` is
absent on this repo's authoring laptop, so the three make entries matched
commands that cannot run there and the allowlist granted nothing: every gate
run and every deploy went back to a prompt. The mirrors are exact -- the same
fixed bodies reached by a different spelling, not a wider grant -- and each
one names a script in this repo that tools/validate_deploy.py audits.
